PCI.BIO: Dr. Angelica Urbina is a Clinical Associate Professor at UTRGV and has been with the Physician Assistant Department since 2016. She received her Doctor of Medical Science in 2025 from the University of Pittsburgh, Master of Physician Assistant Studies (2010) from The University of Texas - Pan American, and Bachelor of Science in Psychology degree (2007) from Texas A&M University. Mrs. Urbina is the program coordinator for the Physician Assistant Career Track (PACT), an early assurance program for high school graduates. She currently works as a local Emergency medicine PA but also has background in Family and Internal Medicine. Dr. Urbina is a mom of five and loves to read and sleep on her spare time.

A free webinar designed to help institutions understand Validation Reviews, a pathway that recognizes strong existing internal quality assurance and professional development processes aligned with QM Essential Standards. This webinar is designed to help you understand your options and identify a practical path forward, whether you’re building internal processes or refining what you already have. You’ll learn:

What Validation Reviews are and how they can support your institutional quality goals.

️ How recognized processes can signal quality and institutional maturity to internal and external stakeholders.

How to assess whether your current QA and professional development efforts are ready for recognition — or where you may need to build capacity.

What you can learn from the success of Alamo Colleges in building a quality assurance process that earned QM Validation Review recognition.

PRESENT.NAME: PAEA Education Forum
PRESENT.TITLE: UnlockED: Hands-On Design of Educational Escape Rooms for PA Programs
PRESENT.ABSTRACT:
UnlockED is an interactive Makerspace Workshop where participants will collaboratively design and prototype an educational escape room aligned with PA learning objectives. Using a structured framework, attendees will apply backward design principles, build puzzles with physical materials, and leave with a transferable escape room blueprint ready for classroom implementation.

Learning Objectives:
Upon completion, participant will be able to describe the core components of an educational escape room, including learning objective alignment, puzzle sequencing, timing, and group flow.

Upon completion, participant will be able to experience and analyze a simplified educational escape room to identify effective design elements related to mechanics, flow, and learner engagement.

Upon completion, participant will be able to apply a structured design blueprint to develop a simplified educational escape room using physical locks and boxes aligned with identified learning objectives.

Upon completion, participant will be able to demonstrate effective facilitation strategies for educational escape rooms, including guiding teamwork, managing time, and supporting learner progression.

Upon completion, participant will be able to identify strategies for adapting and implementing escape rooms within PA curricula to support clinical reasoning, collaboration, and preparation for clinical practice.

PRESENT.NAME: 52nd Annual CME Conference
PRESENT.TITLE: Back to the Pitt
PRESENT.ABSTRACT:
An unforgettable, high-impact educational adventure where emergency medicine meets immersive learning. “Back to the Pitt” is a dynamic, hands-on workshop designed specifically for PA students and early career PAs. Based on the fictional medical drama The Pitt, participants are thrown into a fast-paced ED shift with cases that test their clinical reasoning, teamwork, and time management under pressure.

Created by experienced ED PAs, this workshop weaves real-life emergency cases into collaborative puzzles and clues. Students must work as a team to analyze vitals, interpret diagnostic data, and solve both medical and logic-based challenges to escape before time runs out.

This workshop promotes critical thinking, active learning, and camaraderie—mirroring the high-stakes world of emergency medicine while keeping it engaging and memorable. A short debriefing at the end of the presentation, helps tie up any lose ends and helps solidify the knowledge gained.

Learning Objectives:
1. Identify key clinical findings and red flags in common emergency medicine presentations.
2. Interpret essential diagnostic data such as EKGs, imaging reports, and lab values under time-sensitive conditions.
3. Apply clinical reasoning strategies to solve complex medical cases using a step-by-step team-based approach.
4. Demonstrate effective communication and collaboration skills in a simulated high-pressure clinical environment.
5. Evaluate and prioritize interventions based on evolving patient scenarios to “escape” the emergency shift successfully, Reflect on the experience to identify areas of strength and opportunities for growth in emergency medicine preparedness.

PRESENT.NAME: American Academy of Physician Associates
PRESENT.TITLE: RIA: Enhancing Sports Physical Exam Skills With Video Modules
PRESENT.ABSTRACT:
This presentation is designed for PA educators and clinical faculty interested in innovative teaching strategies. It examines a video-based instructional module developed to improve PA student knowledge and self-efficacy in performing sports pre-participation physical exams. Outcomes demonstrate significant gains in student confidence and clinical readiness, with implications for curriculum design and community-based care.

Learning Objectives:
1. Describe the impact of video-based instruction on PA student knowledge and self-efficacy during sports pre-participation physical examinations.
2. Interpret pre- and post-assessment data to evaluate improvements in clinical readiness and confidence following a video-based educational intervention.
3. Identify strategies for integrating video-based modules into PA curricula to enhance competency-based training and community-focused clinical education.
